asr_text: The legal picture is narrower than the technology picture. The Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons and other mass destruction weapons in orbit and prohibits installing such weapons on the moon and other celestial bodies. It also requires space activity to follow international law, but it does not completely ban every conventional anti-satellite missile, jammer, or cyber operation. United Nations votes in 2024 and 2025 supported existing principles and further arms control work, but they did not create a new comprehensive treaty. The U.S. pledge against destructive direct-assent tests remains a national policy commitment.
